article_title: Non-native insects dominate daytime pollination in a high-elevation Hawaiian dryland ecosystem
version_package_role: byte-transport fallback when legacy per-file stream endpoints fail; provenance must be locked on extracted source files, not the dynamically assembled ZIP container
claim_boundary: This is one Hawaii Island dryland ecosystem containing eight focal native plants. Visitation identity/frequency and manual flower-treatment outcomes must remain distinct. Species within this study are plant-level response panels, not eight independent island systems. Non-native visitor dominance does not by itself establish equivalent pollination service, and contemporary seed-set dependence does not identify historical floral evolution.
